items.snippet: 이재명 대통령은 24일 대학수학능력시험(수능)과 국가자격시험 등 모든 시험의 부정행위에 대해 “사익을 위해 타인에게 심대한 피해를 끼치면서 사회적 신뢰의 근간을 흔든다는 점에서 주가조작 범죄와 본질이 전혀 다르지 않다”고 밝혔다. 이 대통령은 이날 청와대에서 주재한 국무회의에서 “이러한 불법과 반칙을 방관하면 그 사회가 온전하게 유지될 수 없다”며 이같이 말했다. 이어 “정부는 단 하나의 부정행위도 용납하지 않는다는 확고한 원칙 아래 행정력을 총동원해 시험 부정 범죄에 엄정하게 대응해 달라”며 “인공지능(AI) 기업과의 긴밀한 협조, 신고센터 운영 등을 통해 모든 의심 사례를 빠짐없이 추적하고 부정행위에 대해서는 법과 원칙에 따라서 엄정하게 일벌백계해 달라”고 했다. 이 대통령은 “지난 일이니까 이제 다 끝났겠지, 괜찮겠지라는 생각이 명백히...

items.title: 美, 北 해외 노동자 제보에 현상금 500만달러
items.snippet: 미국 국무부가 해외로 파견된 북한 노동자와 이들을 고용하거나 지원하는 대상에 대한 정보에 최대 500만 달러(약 67억 원)의 현상금을 내걸었다. 19일(현지 시간) 미 국무부의 정보 제보 프로그램인 ‘정의를 위한 보상’은 소셜미디어 X를 통해 북한의 해외 노동자 송출과 관련한 정보 제보를 요청했다. 국무부는 “북한 정권이 해외 노동자 착취를 통해 벌어들인 수백만 달러의 자금을 핵무기와 대량살상무기 개발에 사용하고 있다”며 “북한을 지원하는 특정 활동에 관여한 자들의 금융 메커니즘을 차단하는 데 도움이 되는 정보에 최대 500만 달러의 보상금을 지급한다”고 밝혔다. 최근 북한이 자국 노동자의 러시아 및 중국 대규모 파견, 가상화폐 거래소 해킹 등으로 자금 조달에 박차를 가하자 대북 정보 수집에 속도를 내기 위해 현상금 프로그램 홍보에 나선 것...

items.title: 방첩 경험없는 강금실 발탁 논란… 野 “정보전쟁중 보은 인사”
items.snippet: 신임 국가정보원장 후보자에 깜짝 발탁된 강금실 전 법무부 장관을 둘러싼 논란이 확산되고 있다. 방첩·정보 업무 경험이 전무한 강 후보자가 정보 당국 수장을 맡는 게 적절하냐는 지적이다. 중국 지방정부를 위한 활동을 해 온 것을 두고도 우려가 제기된다. 새 국정원장은 한미 정보 협력 난기류를 개선해야 하는 중책을 맡아야 하는 만큼 강 후보자의 이력이 걸림돌이 될 수 있다는 것이다.● “자주파 교체는 美, 姜 발탁은 中 향한 메시지” 보수 야권은 24일 강 후보자의 과거 중국 관련 활동 이력에 대한 공세에 나섰다. 강 후보자는 2013년부터 중국 헤이룽장성 치치하얼시인민정부의 투자유치 특별고문으로 활동했고, 이듬해 치치하얼시를 방문해 중국 당서기를 만나 한국 기업의 현지 유치 방안을 협의했다. 그해 9월엔 중국 지린성 연변조선족자치주정부의 경제특...

items.title: 오세훈 “특검-탄핵 말하자 李 국무회의 끝내”… 한성숙 “민생 논의 자리, 정치적 논쟁 부적절”
items.snippet: 오세훈 서울시장이 24일 국무회의에서 ‘조작기소’ 특별검사와 여권 주도의 조희대 대법원장 탄핵 추진에 대한 발언 기회를 요청했지만 얻지 못했다고 밝혔다. 오 시장이 기자회견을 열어 이런 내용을 밝히자 한성숙 국무총리는 “매우 부적절한 행위”라고 비판했다. 오 시장은 이날 오후 서울시청에서 브리핑을 열고 “오늘 국무회의에서 탄핵과 특검 두 가지에 대해 민심을 대통령께 전달하고 싶었지만 기회를 얻지 못했다”고 말했다. 오 시장에 따르면 국무회의 말미에 발언을 신청하자 이 대통령은 이날 회의 주제와 관련된 내용인지 물었다. 이에 “특검과 탄핵에 관한 민심을 전달드리고자 한다”고 답하자 이 대통령이 곧바로 회의를 마치겠다며 의사봉을 세 번 두드리고 자리를 떴다는 것이다. 오 시장은 ‘조작기소 특검’ 임명 중단과 조 대법원장 탄핵 저지를 요청하는 건의...

items.title: 李, 국무회의서 ‘사이비 종교단체’ 언급 “해산 실효적 조치 검토해야”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령은 24일 종교활동을 빙자해 범죄, 불법 행위를 자행하는 사이비 종교단체에 대한 해산 절차와 관련해 “실효적 조치를 현실적으로 검토할 때가 된 것 같다”고 밝혔다. 더불어민주당 내부에서 신천지 신도 집단 당원 가입 의혹을 둘러싸고 친명(친이재명)계와 친청(친정청래)계가 격돌하는 상황에서 사이비 종교 단체 해산 메시지를 낸 것이다. 이 대통령은 이날 청와대에서 주재한 국무회의에서 사이비 종교단체 해산 절차를 “오래전에 말한 바 있다”면서 “최근까지 온갖 범죄 행위들, 조직 자체를 활용한 불법 범죄 행위가 드러나고 있다”며 이같이 말했다. 이어 “문화체육관광부가 그동안 검토 내용, 현재 상황, 계획 등을 별도로 보고해 달라”고 했다. 이 대통령의 종교단체 발언은 준비된 모두 발언 원고에는 포함된 내용이 아닌 것으로 알려졌다. 이 대통...

items.title: ‘12·3 국민주권의 날’ 지정… 빛의 위원회 내년 예산 79억
items.snippet: 정부가 12·3 비상계엄을 평화적으로 저지한 것을 기리기 위해 매년 12월 3일을 국가 기념일인 ‘국민주권의 날’로 24일 지정했다. 이재명 대통령이 이날 주재한 국무회의에선 ‘각종 기념일 등에 관한 규정’ 개정안이 통과됐다. 이 대통령은 “역사적인 국민주권의 날을 국가기념일로 정해 기리는 것은 나라의 주인은 국민이라는 국민주권 원칙을 다시 한번 확고하게 세우기 위한 것”이라며 “민주주의를 파괴하는 어둠의 세력을 국민 모두의 힘으로 몰아낸 빛의 혁명은 세계 민주주의 역사에 기록될 위대한 국민 승리”라고 했다. 이에 따라 기념일 지정 전에는 민간 단체와 국회 등이 별도로 열었던 비상계엄 해제 기념행사가 정부 주관의 통합 기념식 행사로 치러지게 된다. 다만 국민주권의 날은 공휴일은 아니다. 내년도 정부 예산안에는 대통령 직속 빛의 위원회 관련 예...

items.title: 판사들 “재판 계기 법관 탄핵, 역사 오점” vs “조직 이기주의 비칠 우려”
items.snippet: 더불어민주당이 조희대 대법원장 탄핵을 추진하는 가운데 30일 열리는 전국법관대표회의에 ‘사법부 독립’ 관련 안건은 아직 접수되지 않은 것으로 파악됐다. 사전접수는 23일 밤 12시 마감됐지만 법원 안팎에서 탄핵을 둘러싼 논란이 이어지고 있어 회의 당일 현장에서 관련 안건이 발의될 가능성이 크다는 관측이 나온다. 24일 법관대표회의 임시회의를 위해 사전에 상정된 안건은 인공지능(AI)의 무분별한 활용과 재판소원 등 3건이다. 형사소송법 개정과 법왜곡죄 등에 관한 ‘법원행정처 설명 요청’도 2건 접수됐다. 전날까지 게시된 ‘사법부 독립’ 관련 안건은 1건이었지만 발의자 외에 1명만 동의해 상정되지 못했다. 다만 다른 법관대표 9명 이상의 동의를 얻으면 회의 당일 현장에서 안건 상정을 요구할 수 있어 법관대표회의 당일 탄핵 관련 안건이 논의 대상이...

items.title: 與, 긴급 토론회 열며 ‘曺 탄핵’ 여론전… 내부선 “인용 가능성 있나”
items.snippet: 더불어민주당이 24일 한덕수 전 국무총리에 대한 대법원 판결을 비판하는 긴급토론회를 열고 조희대 대법원장 탄핵 여론전에 나섰다. 당 안팎에서 민주당이 제시한 탄핵 사유들을 놓고 ‘파면을 정당화할 만큼 중대한 헌법·법률 위반에 해당하느냐’는 지적이 나오자 당 차원의 명분 쌓기에 나선 것. 하지만 당내에선 낮은 탄핵 인용 가능성과 역풍을 우려하는 목소리가 이어졌다. 국민의힘은 “사유를 뒤늦게 끼워 맞춘 정략적 탄핵”이라며 반발했다.● ‘韓 판결 토론회’에 與 161명 중 91명 참여 국회에서 ‘한덕수 대법원 판결, 무엇이 문제인가―내란 청산과 국헌 문란의 관점에서’를 주제로 열린 긴급토론회에 참석한 김민석 대표는 한 전 총리에 대한 대법원 판결과 관련해 “무죄 추정의 파기 환송을 했다는 점뿐만 아니라, 비상계엄이 위헌이고 위법하다는 것에 의문의...

items.title: “컨설팅비 10억 요구 거부에 허위 폭로” 장동혁 측 징계 논란 역공… 갈등 확산
items.snippet: 국민의힘 전현직 중앙윤리위원들이 무소속 한동훈 의원과 친한(친한동훈)계 인사들에 대한 ‘조작·하명 징계’ 폭로를 이어가고 있는 가운데 장동혁 대표 측이 역공에 나섰다. 전직 윤리위원이 수억 원을 요구했다가 거부당하자 허위 폭로전을 벌이고 있다고 주장한 것이다. 장 대표 측은 전 윤리위원 최규동 씨가 올해 3월 장 대표 측에 자문단 운영과 컨설팅 명목 등으로 최대 10억 원을 요구했다고 24일 밝혔다. 장 대표 측이 이를 수용하지 않자 황경성 윤리위원과 함께 허위 폭로전에 나섰다는 것. 장 대표가 윤리위원으로 임명했지만 명단 유출 직후 사퇴한 최 씨는 한 의원 제명 당시 장 대표와 주고받은 문자메시지 등을 황 위원을 통해 공개하고 있다. 최 씨는 “10억 원 요구설은 완전 허위 조작”이라며 장 대표를 향해 “‘조작 징계’ 당 대표답다”고 반박했...

items.title: 회견도 없이 100일 맞은 김민석… 정청래, 金 겨냥 글 5건 쏟아내

items.title: 내신 시험서 ‘AI 커닝’ 걸리면 최대 퇴학
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령은 24일 대학수학능력시험(수능) 등 시험 부정행위와 관련해 “지난일이니까 이제 다 끝났겠지, 괜찮겠지라는 생각이 명백히 오산이라는 점을 확실하게 보여줘야 한다”고 말했다. 이 대통령은 이날 국무회의 모두발언에서 “(시험 부정행위는) 타인에게 심대한 피해를 끼치면서 사회적 신뢰의 근간을 흔든다는 점에서 주가조작 범죄와 전혀 다르지 않다”며 행정력을 총동원해 시험 부정 범죄에 엄정하게 대응하라고 했다. 그러면서 “기존의 시험과 평가 방식에 변화가 필요한 건 아닌지도 이제 고민해야 될 때”라고도 했다.

items.title: 국가시험선 ‘수험생은 앞치마, 감독관은 보디캠’
items.snippet: 정부는 앞으로 국가 자격시험에서 ‘AI 커닝’을 막기 위해 모든 수험생에게 일회용 앞치마를 지급하고, CCTV(감시 카메라)가 없는 고사장의 경우 감독관에게 보디캠을 착용하도록 했다. 또 전원이 꺼진 전자 기기도 찾아낼 수 있는 ‘비선형 접합 탐지기’도 도입한다. 부정행위 제재도 강화해 응시 제한은 최대 10년, 형사처벌은 최대 징역 5년으로 높이는 방안을 추진하기로 했다.

items.title: 野 “공소취소 않겠다고 못하나” 이용철 “예”
items.snippet: 이용철 법무부 장관 후보자는 24일 열린 국회 법제사법위원회 인사청문회에서 이재명 대통령 사건 공소취소 문제와 관련해 “국민이 납득하기 어려운 무리한 지휘권을 행사할 생각은 없다”고 밝혔다. 이 후보자는 그러면서도 “공소취소를 지휘하지 않겠다고는 말할 수 없냐”는 물음에는 짧게 “예”라고 답했다. 그는 “청와대로부터 공소취소 요청을 받았냐”는 물음에 “그런 적 없다”고 했다. 법조계에선 이 후보자가 ‘조작기소 특검’ 수사 결과에 따라 공소취소에 나설 가능성을 열어 뒀다는 해석이 나왔다.

items.title: “내가 담근 김장 김치… 맛있어서 자꾸 손이 가네”
items.snippet: 24일 전남광주 운암1동 행정복지센터에서 열린 ‘사랑의 김장 김치 나눔’ 행사에 참가한 서강중학교 학생들이 이웃 250가구에 전달할 김치를 담그고 있다. 한국물가정보에 따르면, 올해는 예년보다 배추·무 등 주요 채소류 작황이 좋아 김장 비용이 2020년대 들어 가장 낮을 것으로 조사됐다.

items.title: 희귀·중증질환자 의료비 본인부담률, 내달부터 10%서 7%로
items.snippet: 다음 달부터 국내 희귀·중증 난치 질환자 약 136만명의 건강보험 본인 부담률이 10%에서 7%로 낮아진다. 이에 따라 환자 한 명당 연평균 본인 부담금이 약 75만원에서 53만원으로 22만원가량 줄어들게 된다.

items.title: 가정폭력 범죄 ‘피해자가 원치 않아도 처벌’ 추진
items.snippet: 청와대는 24일 열린 국무회의에서 가정폭력 범죄에 반의사불벌죄 적용 배제가 필요하다는 의견이 모아졌다고 밝혔다. 현재는 가정폭력 가운데 단순폭행 등은 피해자가 처벌 의사가 있어야 가해자를 처벌할 수 있다. 가족 등 친밀한 관계에서 발생하는 ‘관계성 범죄’도 국가가 처벌하겠다는 뜻이다. 김성완 청와대 대변인은 이날 이재명 대통령 주재로 청와대에서 열린 국무회의 비공개 순서에서 성평등가족부가 마련한 ‘가정폭력범죄 반의사불벌죄 적용 배제 검토’ 방안에 대한 토론이 이뤄졌다며 “가정폭력 범죄의 반의사불벌죄 적용 배제가 필요하다는 데 의견이 모아졌다”고 전했다. 앞서 원민경 성평등가족부 장관은 잇따른 관계성 범죄 등과 관련, 가정폭력 반의사불벌 조항을 폐지해야 한다는 입장을 밝혀왔다.

items.snippet: 프로 무대에 서지 못한 선수들의 도전 스토리로 관심을 모은 서울 ‘서대문구청 여자농구단’이 올해 말 해체된다. 한국 여자농구의 전설 박찬숙 감독이 이끈 이 팀은 2023년 창단 이후 전국체전에서 3년 연속 우승했다. 그러나 지난 7월 구청장이 바뀐 뒤 창단 4년도 안 돼 문을 닫게 됐다. 서대문구는 24일 “재정 여건과 주민들의 생활체육 수요 등을 고려해 여자농구단 운영을 올해 말 종료한다”고 밝혔다. 구는 “농구단 운영 등에 쓰던 예산을 생활체육 프로그램 확대와 문화·체육시설 개선에 투자하겠다”고 했다.

items.title: 故이건희 유족 기부금 5000억 투입… 중앙감염병병원 내년 착공
items.snippet: 고(故) 이건희 삼성 선대회장 유족의 기부금으로 건립하는 중앙감염병병원이 내년 착공에 들어간다. 국립중앙의료원은 국내외 감염병 전문가 300여 명을 초청해 23~24일 진행한 ‘제2회 신종 감염병 의료 대응 국제 심포지엄’에서 이 같은 계획 등을 밝혔다. 앞서 이재용 삼성전자 회장 등 유족은 2021년 소아암·희소질환 환자 지원에 3000억원, 국가 감염병 대응 체계 구축에 7000억원 등 총 1조원을 기부했다. 이 중 5000억원이 음압 병상 150개 규모의 중앙감염병병원 건립에 쓰이는 것이다.

'오딘Q'는 2021년 출시 이후 국내 양대 앱 마켓 매출 1위와 대한민국 게임대상에서 대상을 수상한 '오딘: 발할라 라이징'의 세계관을 계승한 신작이다. 원작은 대만에서도 매출 1위를 기록하는 등 국내외 시장에서 흥행 성과를 거뒀다. 카카오게임즈는 이날 '오딘Q' 공식 티저 페이지를 공개하고 신규 키비주얼을 선보였다.

items.title: Resilience of Entangling Gates to Spatiotemporally Correlated Noise
items.abstract: As quantum processors scale, spatially and temporally correlated noise is emerging as a limiting factor in the fidelity of multiqubit gates. Here we show that this makes the choice of entangling operation a first-order design decision: for two-qubit gates in semiconductor spin qubits, the CZ and $\sqrt{\mathrm{iSWAP}}$ gates exhibit a pronounced resilience to correlated noise relative to the SWAP gate, even though correlated fluctuations of the entangling interaction can degrade gate performance to a level comparable to that of local noise. We trace this hierarchy to the redistribution of noise-sensitive channels away from zero frequency and show it to hold for noise spectra dominated by low-frequency weight, including $1/f$ and Lorentzian. These results follow from a general expression, derived here, for the average gate infidelity under arbitrary spatiotemporal noise correlations, vali...

items.title: Generalized dielectric-dependent hybrid functional combining Gaussian and Yukawa screening
items.abstract: We develop a generalized Coulomb-attenuated method (GCAM) for dielectric-dependent hybrid functionals that combines Gaussian and Yukawa-type screening functions to provide an accurate representation of the random-phase approximation (RPA) dielectric function. Through systematic fitting to RPA dielectric functions of semiconductors and insulators, and to the Lindhard dielectric function of the homogeneous electron gas, we demonstrate that GCAM significantly reduces errors in the model dielectric function across the full momentum range. However, despite this improved physical description of screening, band gap calculations reveal that GCAM yields larger errors compared to experiment than previous CAM approaches for wide-gap materials, but smaller errors for most narrow-gap materials. items.title: Two-dimensional Thyristor
items.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors offer a viable platform for next-generation electronics beyond sub-3 nm nodes, yet essential nonlinear circuit elements, such as thyristors, remain unexplored on atomically thin platforms. Here, we report an atomically thin reconfigurable electro-optical thyristor based on a lateral WSe2-MoSe2-WSe2-MoSe2 PNPN heterostructure, directly grown via sequential edge epitaxy. Unlike single-junction 2D diodes, this multijunction architecture exhibits thyristor-like nonlinear switching, including forward blocking, abrupt snapback, bistability, and electrical latching. The device exhibits a forward-blocking voltage of 183 V, corresponding to a critical electric field of 1 MV/cm. Under open-gate conditions, avalanche-assisted carrier multiplication and regenerative feedback are associated with a sharp forward-voltage drop of 175 V, a pronounced current surge, and...

items.title: A Highly Tunable (Ti,Zr)N$_x$-Based MIM Plasmonic Sensor for Multidomain Biological, Chemical, and Physical Sensing
items.abstract: Metal-Insulator-Metal (MIM) plasmonic refractive index (RI) sensors have attracted considerable attention for label-free, real-time analyte detection; however, their reliance on noble metals such as gold and silver imposes fundamental constraints on tunability, thermal stability, and CMOS process compatibility. In this work, we propose a novel MIM plasmonic RI sensor based on a square ring resonator with embedded circular nanorods, employing the ternary nitride (Ti,Zr)N$_x$ as the plasmonic material, marking its first application in a MIM sensing platform. Compared to binary nitrides and other alternative plasmonic materials reported in the literature, (Ti,Zr)N$_x$ offers broader compositional tunability and greater flexibility in tailoring the optical response while remaining fully CMOS-compatible. The sensor is validated across a comprehensive range of biosensing and physicochemical an...

items.title: Scanning nanowire quantum dot with radio-frequency read-out
items.abstract: Scanning single-electron transistors (SETs) are highly sensitive local probes of charge and electric potential, but their integration with robust height control for scanning probe microscopy remains challenging. Furthermore, readout bandwidths are limited to tens of kHz, while characterizing faster charge dynamics is often of interest. Here, we present a scanning SET in the form of a nanowire (NW) quantum dot (QD) integrated at the apex of a non-contact atomic force microscopy (NC-AFM) cantilever. We demonstrate NC-AFM topographic imaging and local electrometry capability by mapping the electrostatic potential generated by a set of nanoscale voltage-biased gate electrodes. Comparison with electrostatic simulations shows agreement with the measured potential profiles. items.title: Anatomy of orbital and spin responses in GaAs and Si: Hall, inverse Faraday, and magneto-optical Kerr effects
items.abstract: Magneto-optical signals in nonmagnetic semiconductors entangle spin and orbital contributions, both in angular-momentum generation and magneto-optical detection. We calculate these contributions for electron-doped GaAs and Si using density-functional theory, linear-response theory, and a second-order density-matrix treatment of the inverse Faraday effect. At small electron doping, the intrinsic orbital Hall conductivity exceeds its spin counterpart in magnitude, while the orbital contribution to light-induced magnetization dominates over broad photon-energy ranges. We show that orbital- and spin-resolved optical Hall and polar Kerr coefficients exhibit stronger sensitivity to orbital moments than to equal spin moments. items.title: Numerical simulations of CCP-2D GEC with sGMRES
items.abstract: Fluid models provide an efficient means of simulating the low-temperature gas discharges, which are important in semiconductor manufacturing. This work presents, to the best of our knowledge, the first systematic numerical framework for the Gaseous Electronics Conference (GEC) reference cell of the 2D capacitively coupled plasma (CCP). The framework employs a structured, nonuniform cylindrical mesh to resolve the spatial gradients. A semi-implicit Scharfetter-Gummel (SG) scheme is used for the Poisson's equation, while the implicit SG schemes are applied to the continuity equations and the electron energy equation. Both the explicit and and the implicit formulations based on the conventional drift-diffusion terms are also investigated. To solve the resulting large-scale linear systems, we introduce an incomplete LU (ILU)-preconditioned sketched GMRES (sGMRES) method as the solver. As far...

items.title: Strain-driven terahertz phase modulation in piezoelectric and nonlinear optical crystals: mechanisms, material developments, and modulation strategies
items.abstract: Terahertz (THz) technology has witnessed notable developments in sensing, spectroscopy, imaging, and wireless communication which have increased the demand for high-performance THz modulators. Among the various approaches for controlling the THz waves, the application of external stimuli such as optical pumping and thermal or electric fields is widely employed as a promising strategy for modulation. This review focuses on recent advances in THz modulation based on different materials including 2D semiconductors and metamaterials with attention to their response under external stimuli. items.title: Indentation-induced polar domain reconfiguration in the charge-density-wave semiconductor EuTe4
items.abstract: Controlling polar domains in conducting materials by external fields could unlock polarization-based electronic functionalities, yet remains experimentally challenging. While mechanical actuation driven by local strain, stress, or strain gradients has been proposed as an external-voltage-free route, its experimental demonstration in relatively conducting polar materials remains limited. Here we demonstrate mechanically induced polar-domain reconfiguration in the charge-density-wave (CDW) semiconductor EuTe4 at room temperature, whose resistivity is on the order of 10 m$Ω$cm. Polarized-light microscopy and second-harmonic-generation measurements reveal CDW-induced in-plane polarization domains with an approximately 90 $^\circ$ domain configuration. items.title: Proposal for a cat-cluster-state machine gun
items.abstract: Non-Gaussian bosonic states such as the Schrödinger cat states are essential for continuous-variable quantum-information processing. A convenient and deterministic process for generating cat states is through the use of a Rabi interaction between a single bosonic mode and a spin which facilitates a state-dependent displacement. The lack of a Rabi interaction for propagating optical photons has rendered optical cat states elusive. Here, we show that the complex nonlinear scattering dynamics of a single-mode squeezed-vacuum state interacting with a quantum emitter can be engineered to produce a Rabi interaction between a quantum emitter and a propagating photon mode while the contributions from other orthogonal modes destructively interfere. items.title: Population of spin orbit-split-electron branches in semimetallic HgTe quantum wells
items.abstract: We present the results of experimental studies on magnetoresistance, the Hall effect, and Shubnikov-de Haas oscillations performed in gated heterostructures with HgTe-based gapless semiconductor quantum wells. We show that in quantum wells with widths corresponding to a semimetallic charge carrier spectrum, electrons, in contrast to the idealized model, populate both spin-orbit-split branches of the spectrum. This occurs regardless of whether the Fermi level lies exclusively in the conduction band or within the conduction-valence band overlap region.

items.title: AgenticMM: A Material-Centered Multi-Agent Architecture for Scalable First-Principles Materials Modeling
items.abstract: Multi-agent frameworks are attracting increasing attention as a means of autonomously driving complex, long-running workflows in first-principles materials modeling. However, such frameworks commonly organize AI agents by computational task or scientific role. When scaled across many materials, this organization can require repeated transfers of material-specific context and complicate persistent execution and resource coordination. Here, we introduce AgenticMM, a material-centered multi-agent architecture in which each material has a persistent agent that owns its complete workflow and retains its scientific context, while a persistent coordinator allocates shared resources, mediates communication, and tracks campaign progress. items.title: JAX-Nano: A GPU-Accelerated Differentiable Phonon Boltzmann Transport Solver for Nanoscale Heat Transfer
items.abstract: As semiconductor device dimensions approach phonon mean free paths, heat transport enters ballistic and quasi-ballistic regimes where Fourier's law becomes inadequate. The phonon Boltzmann transport equation (BTE) describes these nonequilibrium effects but presents significant computational challenges. This work introduces JAX-Nano, a GPU-accelerated, end-to-end differentiable phonon BTE solver for nanoscale heat transport. The solver integrates steady-state and transient BTE formulations within a unified finite-volume framework, supporting structured and unstructured meshes, mode-resolved transport, phonon scattering, volumetric heat generation, and multiple boundary conditions. Automatic differentiation enables gradient computation with respect to transport properties, boundary conditions, heat-generation rates, and geometric parameters without separately derived adjoint equations. items.title: Multi-Order Passive Macromodeling from Layouts via Nested Port-Hamiltonian Learning
items.abstract: Compact, passive state-space macromodels of interconnects and power-delivery networks are essential for stable transient signal- and power-integrity simulations. However, conventional flows require costly per-layout full-wave electromagnetic (EM) simulations, while both traditional fitting and prior learning surrogates rely on post-hoc fitting or passivity perturbation that degrades accuracy without guaranteeing convergence. In this work, we propose an end-to-end macromodeling framework that learns directly in the passive space, mapping physical layout graphs to multi-order port-Hamiltonian (pH) macromodels. items.title: First-Principles Investigation of the {ScSe2} TMDs Monolayer: Structural Stability, Electronic and Optical Properties
items.abstract: We present an ab initio investigation of the {ScSe2} monolayer using density functional theory (DFT), as employed in the CP2K code, to assess its structural stability and electronic properties. The electronic behavior of both phases is governed by the local coordination environment of scandium and the associated lifting of degeneracy of its $3d$ orbitals. The valence bands (VBs) are dominated by {Se}$-4p$ states in both phases, while the states near the Fermi level distinguish the metallic 1T phase from the semiconducting 2H phase. Optical response calculations reveal markedly different spectral signatures for the two polymorphs. Two findings emerge from this study: a polymorphism-driven metal-to-semiconductor transition without any change in chemical composition and distinct optical responses relevant to phase-selective optoelectronic devices.

items.title: CHARMS250V1: A Cryogenic Front-End ASIC for Low-Noise Readout of Charge or Light Signals in Noble Liquid Detectors
items.abstract: This work presents the design and measurement results of CHARMS250V1, a next-generation cryogenic front-end application specific integrated circuit (ASIC) developed using a 65 nm CMOS process. It is designed for low-noise readout of charge or light signals generated in noble liquid detectors. CHARMS250V1 is a single channel prototype whose design in the future will be integrated within a 16-channel ASIC. It comprises pre-amplification and pulse shaping stages that provide programmable charge gain between 4.3 mV/fC and 25 mV/fC, peaking time programmable between 250 ns and 2 us, and programmable baseline of either 200 mV or 900 mV for processing of unipolar and bipolar signals, respectively.

items.title: Metal to Semiconductor Transition in Niobium Sulfoselenide Alloy Films by Compositional Control
items.abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have garnered significant interest due to their tunable bandgaps, optical anisotropy, and mechanical flexibility. This study explores the relationship between stoichiometry, structural phase, and electronic transport in niobium sulfoselenide (NbSxSe2-x) thin films. In this study, low-dimensional TMD films were grown with molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) to investigate the effects of varying chalcogen (sulfur and selenium) content in NbSxSe2-x alloys. We focus on tuning electrical resistivity along with the transition from metallic-to-semiconducting behavior through compositional control. These MBE grown films were characterized using in-vacuo x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) to analyze the chemical composition. items.title: Optical Scintillation Imaging for Dynamic Source Tracking Dosimetry During Prostate HDR Brachytherapy
items.abstract: High-dose-rate (HDR) brachytherapy is highly conformal, but its accuracy depends on catheter and source placement, and clinical workflows lack real-time in vivo dosimetry (IVD) that verifies delivery without disrupting the procedure. We characterize a scintillator-based optical dosimeter integrated into a transrectal probe that tracks source position, speed, dose rate, and time-resolved cumulative dose. A 67 mm x 5 mm line scintillator is imaged by a CMOS camera through a 30-degree endoscopic lens; geometric and flat-field corrections remove barrel distortion and vignetting. Absolute dose was calibrated with a TOPAS Monte Carlo model of the probe's air-cavity geometry. The system was validated in a water phantom with an Ir-192 source and needles at radial offsets of 7, 10, and 15 mm. items.title: Physical Learning for Autonomous Tuning of Spin Qubits in Electrostatically Defined Quantum Dots
items.abstract: Tuning electrostatically defined quantum dots remains a primary bottleneck in the scalability of semiconductor spin qubits. While existing solutions rely on machine learning algorithms, these approaches require global information, introduce latency bottlenecks, and tax the limited cooling power available at cryogenic stages. Here, we demonstrate an FPGA-in-the-loop learning paradigm that bypasses digital computing overhead by utilizing multiplexed gradient descent (MGD) for tuning. Implemented on an FPGA and an emulated quantum dot device, our system autonomously tracks environmental drift, dynamically recovers from discrete charge jumps, and maintains steady-state stabilization in low signal-to-noise ratio regimes, without prior knowledge of the device's cross-capacitance matrix. items.title: Coherence Lengths of Laser Pointers
items.abstract: We report on the coherence lengths of low-cost green laser pointers in the midst of multimodal behavior using an optical interferometer based on noncollinear beam geometries and a CMOS detector array. Examined devices include three diode lasers and a frequency-doubled neodymium-emission diode-pumped solid state (DPSS) laser. Coherence length measurements are variable among devices, but values can nevertheless regularly exceed 10 cm. The work serves as a template for an advanced undergraduate physics laboratory experiment and may inspire new kinds of laser pointer devices utilizing interference effects as operative principles.

items.title: Specification-Grounded Adaptive Triage and Formal Invariant Exclusion Synthesis for Autonomous Silicon Coverage Closure
items.abstract: Closing the final 5%-15% of code and functional coverage remains a major schedule bottleneck in silicon tapeouts. Existing LLM-based coverage closure loops feed raw uncovered RTL lines or branches directly into iterative prompts, failing on industrial subsystems due to: (1) token and context explosion from querying thousands of correlated holes independently; (2) illegal stimulus that violates cross-signal invariants and yields dirty coverage; and (3) unsafe exclusion hallucination on structurally unreachable dead code. We present ARGUS (Autonomous Reachability & Guided Unified Stimulus), a specification-grounded, dual-regime coverage closure and formal exclusion synthesis engine. items.title: Magnon high-harmonic generation by nonlinearities of spin torque driven by phonon-mediated crossing of many-body energy levels of bright and dark excitons
items.abstract: Recent intense experimental focus on CrSBr, a two-dimensional (2D) antiferromagnetic semiconductor, has revealed numerous surprises in its response to ultrafast optical drive. We demonstrate that a single microscopic mechanism accounts for two of them---high-harmonic generation of magnons and persistence of magnon oscillations over \mbox{$\sim 1$ ns} time scale that is much longer than the femtosecond laser pulse (fsLP) pump duration. This mechanism arises from an unusually complex interplay of four different fundamental quasiparticles of condensed matter physics: magnons, optically bright and dark excitons, and phonons. By viewing magnons as the system and the other three quasiparticles as a quantum many-body bath, we derive an extended Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (eLLG) equation. items.title: From power to spectrum: an off-the-shelf photodiode turned into a spectrometer by its bias alone
items.abstract: Computational spectrometers replace dispersive optics with detectors whose spectral response can be varied, but every reported single-detector device obtains this response through dedicated fabrication: two-dimensional heterostructures, graded epitaxial junctions, organic stacks, filters or photonic circuits. We demonstrate a generic, fabrication-free alternative in which a standard commercial photodiode becomes a spectrometer through its electrical drive alone, requiring no modification of the device, no optical filter and no modulation of the light. The mechanism is bias-modulated optoelectronic chromatic dispersion (OED): light of different wavelengths is absorbed at different depths, and a sinusoidal bias changes how carriers generated at each depth are collected, so that every spectrum is encoded in the shape of the photocurrent waveform over one bias period. items.title: Sliding-ferroelectric control of dipolar and quadrupolar excitons in R-stacked WSe$_2$
items.abstract: A fundamental property of interlayer excitons is their dipolar character, enabling electrical tunability, enhanced exciton-exciton interactions and extended lifetime. It is important for studying collective phenomena and realizing novel optoelectronic devices. However, in homo- or heterostructures based on two-dimensional semiconductors, the magnitude and orientation of the dipole moment are commonly locked due to spatially confined charges and nature of the band transition. Here, we use gate-dependent photoluminescence of few-layer R-WSe2 to harness sliding ferroelectricity for controlling the exciton dipole configuration of emerging layer-hybridised excitons. The sliding-ferroelectric control enables a pronounced on/off switching of the diffusive transport of hybrid dipolar excitons, while further facilitating gradual and abrupt dipole reconfigurations with emerging quadrupolar exciton...

items.title: Topology-Enabled Self-Verification of Quantum Hall Resistance Standards
items.abstract: The scaling of multi-element quantized Hall array resistance standards necessitates rigorous validation that internal quantization has not broken down without relying on the verification of dissipationless edge state transport. One proposed solution is to use a Symmetric Precision Quantization Reliability criterion, a mathematical framework that statistically assures such validation strictly through outer terminal measurements of Cn-symmetric designs. This criterion essentially bounds the likelihood of hidden localized defects arising from quantum Hall breakdown and has potential uses in quantum computing and semiconductor testing but is presented in the context of its application toward quantum electrical standards.

items.title: Thermal investigation of buffer and transition layers in AlGaN HEMT stacks
items.abstract: In this work, we investigate thermal transport in a set of thin-film layers used in modern HEMT designs. Our theoretical analysis employs three phonon-transport models of increasing sophistication, ranging from a relatively simple Debye-approximation model to a first-principles framework that incorporates Density Functional Theory (DFT)-derived harmonic and anharmonic phonon properties. To describe ternary semiconductors, alloy scattering is also considered, and to account for the properties of non-ideal, polycrystalline thin films, scattering at grain and film boundaries is taken into account. For modeling the specific samples at hand, the latter are fitted to thermal conductivity data measured with Time-Domain Thermoreflectance (TDTR). Overall, we find that the first-principles model performs best and produces the most physically consistent results. Special emphasis is placed on establ...

items.title: CRAFT: Analog Circuit Design by Reasoning LLM Agents from Pre-Computed Lookup Tables
items.abstract: Automated analog circuit sizing methods, from black-box optimizers to recent large language model (LLM) agents, typically search the design space with a SPICE simulator in the loop, whereas an experienced designer works out a design by hand analysis. This paper presents CRAFT, a flow in which an LLM agent designs a given topology by calculation, as a designer does, and without an initial sizing. The agent works only through DeX, a service that uses pre-computed lookup tables to provide device characteristics and to solve the whole netlist for its operating point and small-signal response. It thus designs without SPICE, and every final design is verified independently in HSPICE. We test CRAFT on four circuits in a commercial 28 nm process; the largest is a 37-transistor three-stage amplifier with 53 design variables, 20 specifications and 74 saturation constraints. items.title: FlashX: Scaling Robotic Experience Reuse for Embodied Agents with CBA-Based NAND Flash
items.abstract: Embodied agents are emerging as a promising paradigm for complex robotic tasks, leveraging Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and World Action Models (WAMs) to generate actions through Diffusion Transformer (DiT)-based iterative denoising. However, existing models often struggle to generalize to out-of-distribution (OOD) environments. We observe that retrieving successful experiences and using them to warm-start denoising enables agents to better adapt to unfamiliar situations while reducing computational overhead. This creates a new opportunity to improve task accuracy and inference efficiency simultaneously, in contrast to conventional acceleration techniques that trade accuracy for computation. items.title: Origin and hole-density dependence of the intrinsic spin Hall conductivity in inorganic halide perovskites
items.abstract: Metal halide perovskites have spin-orbit coupling among the strongest in semiconductors, yet whether their centrosymmetric bulk phases can convert charge current into spin current, and what controls the response, is unknown. Here we identify, from first-principles calculations on the four all-inorganic compounds CsBX3 (B = Pb, Sn; X = Br, I), the factors that govern their intrinsic spin Hall conductivity. The conductivity arises from the spin Berry curvature of the spin-orbit-split halide-p bands, 1.1-2.6 eV below the valence band maximum, and exceeds that of III-V and group-IV semiconductors when the Fermi level lies inside them. Because the valence band maximum is an s-p singlet, shifted only in second order, these contributions cancel in the undoped compounds, which respond like conventional semiconductors. items.title: Interfacing Silicon Nitride Nanophotonics with Cuprous Oxide Rydberg Excitons
items.abstract: Rydberg excitons in cuprous oxide (Cu$_2$O), the solid-state counterpart of Rydberg atoms, are hydrogen-like electron--hole quasi-particles with micron-sized wavefunctions and strong long-range interactions that promise optical nonlinearities at the few-photon level. Exploiting them in a waveguide quantum electrodynamics (WQED) setting can enable what atomic Rydberg platforms achieve only with ultrahigh vacuum and laser cooling/trapping---a guided optical mode interfaced with the Rydberg medium---while adding the scalability and advanced fabrication of integrated photonics. Here we demonstrate a monolithic, CMOS-compatible interface of Cu$_2$O Rydberg excitons with a SiN$_x$ nanophotonic waveguide. items.title: Asymmetric Transistor Aging Under Thermal Gradients
items.abstract: Advanced technology nodes improve performance but increase susceptibility to BTI-induced aging. Using aging- aware circuit simulations, we show that realistic on-chip thermal gradients can cause significant asymmetric transistor degradation in 16 nm FinFET circuits, leading to setup and hold time violations. These results highlight the necessity of incorporating thermal-gradient-aware aging analysis into timing signoff to ensure chip reliability.

items.title: Design and Modeling of Graded Base III-Nitride HBTs for High-Frequency Applications
items.abstract: This work analyzes the high-frequency performance constraints of AlGaN/GaN heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) and proposes a novel band-engineered graded base N-polar AlGaN/GaN HBT and evaluates the RF performances. Unlike conventional p-GaN base designs, we propose a graded base in the N-polar orientation which offers polarization-induced hole accumulation with quasi-electric field-assisted minority carrier transport. The proposed design simultaneously mitigates the longstanding current crowding, Webster effect, and conventional base resistance limitations. Using well-calibrated two-dimensional TCAD simulations, the proposed compositionally graded base HBT projects peak f_T/f_{MAX} of 190/200 GHz with a power density (V_{BR}I_{MAX}/8 > 20 W/mm), offering a promising pathway toward simultaneous high-frequency and high-power GaN millimeter-wave electronics.

items.title: Optical readout of MicroPattern Gaseous Detectors with SiPMs
items.abstract: Scintillation light readout of MicroPattern Gaseous Detectors (MPGDs) is used for imaging and track reconstruction applications including in optical Time Projection Chambers (TPC). Typically, high resolution CCD or CMOS imaging sensors are used and PMTs can be employed to obtain auxiliary timing information. We report on the optical readout of MPGDs with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs) which enables limited spatial resolution. Arrays of SiPMs were used to read out Gaseous Electron Multipliers (GEMs) and Glass Micromegas amplification stages. Center of gravity reconstruction of hit positions yields a spatial resolution of approximately 1.35 mm for signals shared across multiple SiPMs. High gain of the amplification stage as well as the SiPMs enables good signal sharing and is advantageous for position reconstruction.

items.title: Reliable arithmetic circuits using less reliable (sub-digital) logic
items.abstract: The frequent static failure of CMOS logic gates at ultra-low voltages has historically been perceived as a strict barrier to extreme voltage scaling: this paper introduces a statistical circuit law proving this intuition wrong. We discovered a universal power law connecting gate and circuit static failure probabilities, revealing that circuit failure requires the simultaneous breakdown of an entire gate cluster rather than a single component. Because the required cluster size increases rapidly as voltage drops, low-voltage \textit{sub-digital} logic exhibits surprising inherent resilience to static failure. This insight stems from new theoretical tools we developed to quantify static failure, extending well beyond conventional voltage-margin analysis. Consequently, sub-digital processors could potentially offer a viable, near-term solution to drastically reduce the energy demands of AI.

items.abstract: We study a network of three synchronized chaotic lasers and the radio frequency spectra of the intensity fluctuations. The inverse of the delay mismatch between each pair of lasers introduces characteristic frequencies that shape the spectral response of the synchronized system. By studying two different three-laser configurations, we find that peaks appear whenever multiple harmonic contributions overlap in frequency, resulting in constructive enhancement of the spectral power. items.title: Ultrafast Successive Control and Electrical Detection of Long-Lived Valley Polarization in Room-Temperature Germanium
items.abstract: Germanium (Ge) hosts four degenerate valleys in the conduction band minima, and their highly anisotropic effective masses offer a valley degree of freedom in transport phenomena via anisotropic conductivity. Using time- and polarization-resolved terahertz spectroscopy combined with deformation potential theory, we reveal a valley relaxation time reaching 10 ps near the band edge of Ge(001) at room temperature, long enough to detect the valley polarization in electrical transport measurements. We also demonstrate sub-picosecond complete reversal of valley polarization by off-resonant light pulses at extremely low energy consumption. These results pave the way for room-temperature valleytronics based on bulk indirect-gap semiconductors compatible with existing electronics.

items.title: Fault-tolerant quantum processor with minimal external control
items.abstract: Contemporary classical information processors integrate tens of billions of transistors printed on a chip, yet are fully controlled through comparatively few external wires. This is possible because data flows through hard-coded operations in step with a global clock and is steered by external instructions. Today's solid-state quantum processors are different -- every qubit receives instructions from outside the chip via its own dedicated control line, and error correction adds a further torrent of syndrome data that is transported off-chip. Here we show that the external control of a quantum chip can be greatly simplified. We propose a fault-tolerant architecture for universal quantum computation, inspired by modern classical processors, in which quantum information flows through a fixed, clocked device, propelled by local gates in a planar array. items.title: Tuning spreading transport in GaN HEMTs with an AlN space layer under non-equilibrium heating
items.abstract: Lateral spreading transport dominates near-junction heat dissipation in GaN high-electron-mobility transistors, yet thermal control has largely overlooked this geometry. It neither reaches the core AlGaN/GaN region nor, beyond the spatial spreading itself, accounts for the spectral non-equilibrium of the heat source. Here we tune the spreading resistance directly by inserting a thin, highly conducting AlN space layer above the source to intercept heat and divert it laterally. We test this approach across GaN, AlGaN/GaN, and AlGaN/AlN/GaN structures under both equilibrium and longitudinal-optical (LO)-pumped non-equilibrium heating, pairing non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (NEMD) with full-band phonon Monte Carlo (MC). items.title: Breaking the Myth of Four-Tier Stacked Transistors for Logic: an Investigation from Process to Device and Block-Level PPA
items.abstract: For the first time, this work evaluated whether 4-tier stacked transistors can translate the straightforward density gains into realistic chip-level scaling benefits. A practical dual-sided 4-tier transistor-stacking CFFET (Flipped CFET-to-CFET) process was proposed, on which a DTCO framework spanning standard-cell design, local interconnects, RO analysis, and physical implementation was built under 2A node design rules. The CFFET was also benchmarked with its 2-tier transistor-stacking counterparts FFET. Among CFFET configurations, the best-performing Symmetric Power still lags FFET by 11.2% in RO frequency due to the complex MOL parasitics. At the block level, CFFET reduces the Ibex RISC-V core area by only 12.8% (far below the 40% nominal cell-height reduction), while running 10.9% slower at iso-power. items.abstract: Coupled oscillator Ising hardware can produce different solution qualities across repeated runs of the same problem, while a deterministic behavioral model used for the design yields a single outcome under fixed conditions. Capturing this stochastic variability during design time is essential for evaluating how closely simulation reflects silicon behavior. This work presents a probabilistic behavioral RTL simulation framework that introduces Gaussian timing variation into coupling delays. This variation changes oscillator timing during evolution, producing different outcomes across runs while retaining the existing chip control and readout blocks. The framework is evaluated against measurements from two chips: a 28-nm CMOS chip with 66 spins and a 16-nm FinFET chip with 49 spins, using 250 problems run 100 times repetitively. items.title: ADSPICE: A Method of Automatic Differentiation for Gradient-Based Lumped Circuit Optimization with Native SPICE
items.abstract: This work presents a novel computer-aided design (CAD) tool for gradient-based circuit optimization using SPICE and automatic differentiation, which we term ADSPICE. Automatic differentiation (AD) is a technique for evaluating a derivative by breaking it into its elementary differentiation operations and repeatedly applying the chain rule, in contrast with a finite-difference-based derivative computed from a small perturbation. Native SPICE (realized with ngspice) is equipped with automatic differentiation toward gradient-based optimization, particularly adjoint-mode optimization. This is implemented with custom C code and shared library control, allowing easy integration with existing SPICE infrastructure. items.title: Trapped fermions frustrate multiterminal Josephson networks
items.abstract: Coherent control of fermions has become a standard approach for engineering quantum devices. Here, we explore parity-induced frustration in multiterminal Josephson arrays. We focus on odd-parity Josephson trijunctions, where the presence of a trapped fermion induces a phase winding in each trijunction. Connecting these trijunctions constrains their shared phases, resulting in a long-distance phase coherence where the frustrated configurations dominate the low-energy physics. In the classical regime, these arrays map onto the Kagome XY antiferromagnet, whose established Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition yields algebraically decaying $6e$ phase correlations. We show that the $6e$ phase coherence is manifested as a pronounced third harmonic in the current-phase relation of these arrays. items.title: Frequency Multiplexing of Purcell-Enhanced Optically Coherent NV Centers
items.abstract: Integrating optically coherent quantum emitters into nanophotonic structures is key to scalable quantum networks. Realizing them with nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond is hindered by the degradation of optical coherence accompanying nanofabrication. Here, we overcome this challenge by integrating multiple NV centers into a monolithic diamond photonic crystal nanocavity while preserving near-lifetime-limited optical coherence. We observe linewidths as narrow as 19 MHz, enabling the frequency multiplexing of spectrally distinct NV centers within a common cavity mode, while maintaining charge-state stability over several minutes under resonant excitation. Tuning the cavity into resonance with the NV zero-phonon line enhances the optical emission, consistent with Purcell enhancement predicted by finite-element simulations. In this work, we study routing in these recently proposed inter-chiplet interconnect topologies by categorizing and evaluating nine deadlock-free routing functions for irregular topologies known from data center networking in this new context. items.title: Development of a Discrete Variable Representation of a Field-Adaptive Hermite Basis for Accurate Modeling of Magnetically Confined Systems
items.abstract: Accurate magnetic-field evolution of spectra requires a common wavefunction representation that consistently describes multiple states across different field regimes. Discrete Variable Representation (DVR) methods combine accurate basis-based kinetic-energy evaluation with flexible real-space potential representation, enabling arbitrary non-analytic potentials to be treated. Here, we develop a magnetic-field-dependent Hermite function-based (Hermite-B) DVR that adapts naturally to magnetic confinement, efficiently representing compressed wavefunctions across a wide range of field strengths while remaining centered in regions relevant to the scalar confinement potential. This ensures accurate treatment of the field-dependent kinetic energy while addressing two key challenges: maintaining accuracy from the Zeeman to Landau regimes and accommodating diverse confinement potentials. items.title: How well does graph superoptimization transfer? Adapting tensor-graph superoptimizer to a Triton-based NPU
items.abstract: For automatic optimization systems, performance portability across increasingly diverse AI accelerators remains a challenge. We investigate how well graph-level superoptimization transfers across architectures by adapting Mirage from its CUDA-oriented design to the Huawei Ascend 910B3 through a Triton-based compilation stack. We evaluate the adapted system on transformer-relevant workloads, including matrix multiplication, softmax, RMSNorm+MatMul, gated MLP, FNN, and attention. The results show that graph-level optimization can successfully transfer and outperform available reference implementations by up to 87.0% on fused workloads. However, performance is highly dependent on tensor shape and workload structure, with substantial regressions for other configurations. items.title: Performance limits and benchmarking of ideal 2D topological insulator field-effect transistors
items.abstract: Topological insulator field-effect transistors (TIFETs) have emerged as a promising alternative to overcome the scaling limits of silicon-based field-effect transistors (Si-based FETs). In this study, we establish the performance limits of ideal TIFETs and present a comprehensive benchmarking of the switching energy-delay performance of TIFETs against Si-based FETs (FinFET and LGAA) and 2-D material-based FETs ($\mathrm{MoS}_2$ and InSe) under equivalent and realistic conditions. Furthermore, we analyze the key factors influencing the switching energy-delay performance of TIFETs, including contact resistance ($R_{\mathrm{C}}$), parasitic capacitance ($C_{\mathrm{par}}$), channel length ($L$), and channel width ($W$). items.title: Sub-electron noise with a buried-channel DePFET: characterisation of novel DePFET concepts
items.abstract: Depleted P-channel Field Effect Transistor (DePFET) pixel sensors combine Fano-limited energy resolution with fast, low-noise readout and are used in instruments ranging from particle tracking to X-ray astronomy. items.abstract: The generation and control of circularly polarized and chiral light is important for a wide range of applications, from sensing to optical communication and catalysis. Generally, the generation of chiral light emission from plasmonic nanostructures relies on the use of nanoantennas with predefined chiral shape, which requires complex nanofabrication. In this work, we show how localized electron excitation controls the generation of circularly polarized- and chiral cathodoluminescence from a single achiral plasmonic nanoantenna. We exploit the $π$/2 phase difference between the transverse and longitudinal components of the electric field that is carried by 30 keV electrons, to coherently excite degenerate dipolar modes of which the far-field radiation interferes in the far field, thereby creating a strong optical spin-Hall effect. items.title: Koopmans spectral functionals for excitons in materials
items.abstract: Accurate first-principles characterization of excitons typically relies on the Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE) combined with quasiparticle energies from computationally demanding GW calculations. Here, we replace the GW step with quasiparticle energies from Koopmans-compliant spectral functionals, an approach we call BSE@qKI, and implement it in an automated, reproducible AiiDA workflow. For a set of benchmark semiconductors, BSE@qKI reproduces experimental band gaps and first exciton energies with mean absolute relative errors of 13% and 4%, respectively, comparable to BSE@G0W0 for the gaps and markedly better for the excitation energies. We also apply the method to the layered magnetic semiconductor CrI3, obtaining an absorption spectrum that reproduces the main experimental features. These results establish BSE@qKI as a GW-free alternative to BSE@G0W0 for systematic studies of excitonic...

items.title: A Discrete Digital Isolator with Shielded Planar Transformer for Gate Driver Applications
items.abstract: Galvanically isolated gate drivers are required in many power electronics applications. This paper describes an implementation of a digital isolator using discrete components with a planar coreless PCB signal transformer providing the isolation. The use of an electrostatic shield between the transformer windings is shown to provide sufficient common-mode transient immunity to support IGBT half-bridge drivers, an application subject to a severe dV/dt transient during switching. The design is verified through the experimental implementation of a prototype half bridge using two of the proposed discrete digital isolators with SiC power transistors and demonstrates common-mode transient immunity greater than 15 kV/us with very low implementation complexity.

items.title: Computed Permutation Trellis Coding: Near-Optimal Quantization from Two Multiplications and a 64-Byte Table
items.abstract: We propose Computed Permutation Trellis Coding (CPTC), a low-bit quantization format for tensors written once and read many times. Formats that round each value on its own, such as INT4 and FP4, waste a large part of their bits against the information-theoretic ideal. Trellis codes recover this loss by encoding values jointly, but prior decoders either need a large lookup table for their best quality or compute values with a hash that restricts what they can decode. CPTC's decoder multiplies its state by two coefficients and adds the top bits of the products to index a 64-byte table. Because that sum is not uniformly distributed, the rarely used ends of a small table can hold values far out in the tails. One decoder serves every bit width from 1 to 6, reproduces the standard integer and floating-point formats exactly, and comes within 0.07 bits of the ideal at 4 bits. It matches a random...

items.title: Photonic Maxwells demon as an energy resource
items.abstract: We propose a new realization of Maxwells demon for photons and its use as an energy resource. The starting point is a multilayer dielectric mirror that transmits photons within a certain wavelength band but reflects photons at longer wavelengths, followed by a material that irreversibly converts the wavelength. A 3D box constructed from these one-way mirrors is a self-acting Maxwells demon for photons. The first case considered is a one-way mirror for visible photons, converting blue to red as an example. The next case is a one-way mirror that transmits visible light but reflects infrared light, followed by a perfect blackbody. We analyze a 3D box with such mirrors as walls to accumulate and store blackbody radiation. Applications include solar-powered thermal energy and solar-powered thermophotovoltaics. items.title: Controlling Mode-Locking in Liquid Light
items.abstract: Mode-locking is the process by which the phases of many cavity modes organize collectively into a stationary state. In lasers, mode-locking originates from the interplay of gain, loss, dispersion and nonlinearities, most commonly resulting in the emission of short pulses. However, pulse formation is prevented when the gain recovery is fast enough to suppress amplitude fluctuations. Mode-locking then produces an extended state of nearly constant intensity, whose dynamics is governed by the phase. Yet, a general framework for designing the phase of such extended photonic states remains lacking. Here we introduce a hydrodynamic approach to designing extended photonic states, in which the phase dynamics are understood and controlled as a flow of liquid-like light. The intensity, clamped by fast gain, plays the role of a constant density, the instantaneous frequency that of a flow velocity, a...

items.title: A Neural Physics Solver for Richards Equation
items.abstract: A new approach to discretise and solve Richards equation based on the finite element method (FEM) is presented. The novelty of the approach, called the Neural Physics method, is that it expresses the discretisation as a convolution neural network (CNN) whose weights are predetermined by the integrals of the basis functions in the FEM. The Neural Physics method is physically consistent as it represents a discretisation of the governing equation and can run on CPUs, GPUs and the latest AI accelerators, resulting in an increase in computational speed. The Neural Physics method is demonstrated for two different discretisations of Richards equation, including a multigrid method that is realised through a U-Net architecture. The accuracy and speed of these methods is tested on a problem with a known analytical solution and compared to a standard FEM, and shows that the Neural Physics method is...

items.title: Near-Quantum-Limited Readout for the Princeton Axion Search using a sub-GHz Kinetic Inductance Traveling Wave Parametric Amplifier
items.abstract: Parametric amplifiers are a workhorse for near-quantum-limited measurements above 1 GHz. However, amplifier development has been more limited below 1 GHz. We present a kinetic inductance traveling-wave parametric amplifier (KI-TWPA) operating over 300-700 MHz, with gain exceeding 30 dB and pump powers of a few hundred nanowatts. The system noise performance, as measured by a variable-temperature noise source, is 2.5-3.5 quanta. This device is a versatile new tool for precision measurements of sub-GHz signals, with applications including readout of semiconductor spin qubits, superconducting detector arrays, and searches for new physics beyond the Standard Model. We characterize aspects of the amplifier performance relevant to axion searches, including gain drift, compression point, amplifier noise at various operating temperatures, readout with an input circulator, and magnetic field inse...

items.title: I$_4$ complex acting as near-infrared emitter with a quantum memory in silicon
items.abstract: Silicon color centers emitting in the near infrared offer a route to spin--photon interfaces compatible with mature complementary metal--oxide--semiconductor fabrication. A key unresolved candidate is the X-line at 1039.7 meV in the photoluminescence (PL) spectrum, long attributed to a complex of four self-interstitials (I$_4$), yet whose microscopic structure and spin properties have remained controversial and uncharacterized at a predictive level. Using hybrid-functional (HSE06) density functional theory, we unambiguously establish the bare I$_4$ complex as the origin of the X-line: our calculations quantitatively reproduce the zero-phonon line, the complete phonon sideband structure---identifying the prominent secondary peaks as one- and two-phonon replicas of strongly coupled quasi-local modes---and the EPR hyperfine constants. The charge transition level is found at VBM$+$0.08~eV, c...

items.title: Revealing New Leakage Paths in GAAFETs using Predictive First-Principles Simulations
items.abstract: Gate-All-Around Field-Effect Transistors (GAAFETs) are emerging as successors to Fin Field-Effect Transistors (FinFETs) and are central to continued scaling at advanced semiconductor nodes. Despite their improved electrostatic control, recent measurements show that the drain current in GAAFETs deviates strongly from thermionic behavior at negative gate voltages, increasing as the gate voltage becomes more negative. This leakage has been attributed to direct gate-drain tunneling through the high-$k$ dielectric, enhanced by drain-induced dielectric barrier lowering (DIDBL). Here, we use predictive, charge-self-consistent Non-Equilibrium Green Function (NEGF) simulations based on the Contact Block Reduction (CBR) method to spatially resolve this leakage pathway in GAAFETs. Unlike approaches based primarily on phenomenological leakage models, our first-principles, multi-terminal quantum-tran...

items.title: BROAD: Bit-Parallel Row-Oriented Arithmetic in DRAM
items.abstract: Processing-using-memory (PUM) architectures perform computation directly within DRAM to reduce costly data movement between memory and processors. Because charge-sharing operations are confined to individual bitlines, existing DRAM-PUM architectures reorganize data into column-oriented, bit-serial representations. This organization is fundamentally incompatible with the row-oriented, word-parallel layouts used by conventional processors and accelerators, requiring expensive data-layout transformations whenever computation transitions between PUM and conventional execution. In this paper, we present BROAD, or Bit-Parallel Row-Oriented Arithmetic in DRAM. BROAD augments the DRAM subarray with two lightweight extensions: migration cells that enable localized horizontal data movement between neighboring bitlines and inversion cells that provide efficient in-array logical inversion. These pri...

items.title: SPLASH: Co-Designing Flash-Aware Sparse Attention with a Virtualized HBM-HBF Hierarchy
items.abstract: As context lengths, request lifetimes and concurrency grow, the key-value (KV) cache dominates memory usage in large language model (LLM) inference. High-bandwidth memory (HBM), the memory on contemporary GPUs, achieves far higher bandwidth than off-package memory, yet its capacity, bounded by DRAM density, has not kept pace with this demand. High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF), an emerging memory technology, bridges this gap, combining the advanced packaging of HBM with the density of flash to deliver terabyte-scale capacity at HBM-class read bandwidth. Exploiting this capacity for long-context KV caches, however, requires hiding the vastly different physical characteristics of flash from the GPU while keeping decode interactive. We therefore introduce Splash, an architecture that virtualizes HBM and HBF for the KV cache. We architect custom HBM and HBF base dies with novel memory and flash cont...

items.title: Probing proximity-induced superconductivity in bilayer graphene using gate-defined quantum dots
items.abstract: Van der Waals heterostructures enable the combination of two-dimensional (2D) materials with different electronic properties in a single device. Bilayer graphene (BLG) is particularly attractive as its electrically tunable band gap enables local control of tunnel barriers and quantum dots (QDs). Here, we realize an all-2D hybrid platform based on BLG proximitized by superconducting NbSe$_2$. Using electrostatic gates, we define tunnel barriers and QDs at different distances from the superconductor-semiconductor interface. The QDs serve as local spectroscopic probes of the proximitized BLG channel, forming tunable superconductor-quantum dot-normal conductor junctions. Coulomb blockade and finite-bias spectroscopy reveal a proximity-induced superconducting gap of up to $80\,\mathrm{μeV}$ and allow to track its evolution with distance from the NbSe$_2$ contact. The local density of states r...

items.title: Continuous-Wave Operation at 30 MV/m of a Superconducting Radio-Frequency Gun Cryomodule with an Exchangeable Cathode Plug
items.abstract: A prototype 185.7 MHz superconducting radio-frequency (SRF) electron gun cryomodule has been developed for the proposed LCLS-II-HE Low Emittance Injector at SLAC. It has an in-situ ultra-high-vacuum exchangeable cathode plug system compatible with semiconductor photocathodes. With a copper plug, the gun achieved continuous-wave RF operation at a cathode field of 30 MV/m. No measurable degradation was observed after plug removal and reinsertion with the cavity at 4.4 K. This result is a significant improvement over past continuous-wave SRF gun systems with exchangeable plugs.

items.title: Heteroepitaxial Growth of PbSe on InP via III-V Buffer Layers
items.abstract: Detector cost remains a barrier to the widespread adoption of mid-wave infrared (3-5 micron) technology. PbSe, an inexpensive narrow band gap IV-VI semiconductor that has been used since the early 1940s, delivers high performance for infrared detection despite the abundance of grain boundaries in polycrystalline films. Epitaxial growth, however, could provide superior crystalline quality and interfaces, but suitable substrates remain limited for PbSe. Recent PbSe heteroepitaxy has focused primarily on III-V, II-VI and group-IV substrates that each offer a comparatively narrow range of lattice-matched alloys for heterostructure engineering. Here we show that InP-based heteroepitaxy provides access to a broader materials platform while limiting the lattice mismatch with PbSe to approximately 4%. We grow 151-nm thick PbSe films by molecular beam epitaxy on 200-nm thick In0.53Ga0.47As and In...

items.title: Thermoelectric properties of metal-semiconductor percolation composites
items.abstract: We analyze the thermoelectric response of composite materials comprising homogeneous semiconductor hosts with randomly distributed metallic inclusions. We demonstrate that the properties of such materials are strongly affected by the percolation transition (with background conductivity). We show that in the vicinity of the percolation threshold, the power factor and the thermoelectric figure of merit strongly depend on both the concentration and arrangement of inclusions. Finally, we identify promising regimes for enhancing the power factor in realistic composites.

items.title: Density-gradient effect in high-harmonic generation in gases
items.abstract: High-harmonic generation (HHG) in gaseous targets is the most widespread method to produce coherent extreme-ultraviolet (XUV) pulses with sub-femtosecond duration. However, this process has intrinsically low efficiency, and substantial research and development is devoted worldwide to increase the achievable photon flux through this highly nonlinear light--matter interaction process. In this work, we show the strong interplay of phase matching and absorption in gas-pressure gradients, substantially affecting macroscopic HHG efficiency. Through detailed experimental analysis and supporting numerical studies, we highlight their significance, particularly at the boundaries of the interaction volume. The concluded results have implications in the massively expanding application possibilities of HHG sources requiring high photon flux, for example in the semiconductor industry, in nanoscale ima...

items.title: Josephson effect in bipolar magnetic semiconductors
items.abstract: We theoretically investigate equilibrium currents in a one-dimensional Josephson junction incorporating a bipolar magnetic semiconductor (BMS). We show that the intrinsic exchange splitting of the spin-resolved bands enables purely electrical control of the $0$--$π$ transition through gate-tunable modulation of the BMS chemical potential, eliminating the need for an external magnetic field. This provides a viable route toward electrically tunable $π$-junction behavior and highlights the potential of BMS-based Josephson devices for phase-controllable superconducting electronics. Furthermore, in the presence of Rashba spin--orbit coupling, we find an anomalous Josephson effect characterized by a finite equilibrium supercurrent at zero phase difference. items.title: OpenTherm: A Unified and Progressive Benchmark for 2.5D/3D-IC Thermal Prediction
items.abstract: Accurate and efficient chip thermal prediction is essential for advanced packaging design. In recent years, deep learning-based thermal predictors have made significant progress, achieving high prediction accuracy while substantially reducing computational costs. However, differences in datasets, simulators, and evaluation protocols hinder direct comparison of existing methods and systematic assessment of their generalization across design variations and cross-package transfer scenarios. We introduce OpenTherm, an open benchmark combining 32,000 established 3D-IC samples with 50,000 new 2.5D chiplet samples generated with the open-source HotSpot simulator. It provides fixed data splits, a common input representation, and shared evaluation tools. Five deployment-aligned Generalization Scopes cover fixed-design workload prediction, within-family layout, material, and cooling exploration, a...

items.title: Dual-Mode Exciton Coupling in Epitaxially Registered Organic-Inorganic 2D Heterocrystals
items.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) heterocrystals comprising molecules and semiconductors can serve as an ideal platform for studying interfacial excitons and for future optoelectronic applications, yet the energy and charge flow across these atomically sharp interfaces remain unclear. In this work, we investigated PTCDA-MoS2 as a prototypical 2D organic-inorganic heterostructure and revealed dual-mode exciton coupling between the constituent crystals. Monolayer-resolved PTCDA molecular crystals were grown on monolayer MoS2 via physical vapor assembly, and their crystallographic details, including the stacking angle, were determined by electron diffraction. Upon the formation of the heterostructures, PTCDA's photoluminescence was completely quenched because of organic-to-inorganic hole transfer, whereas that of MoS2 increased markedly with PTCDA thickness. Using differential reflectance and photolumin...

items.title: First-principles carrier mobility and optical absorption of strained ZnO with self-consistent Hubbard interactions
items.abstract: Carrier mobility and optical absorption are key performance parameters of oxide semiconductors in transparent and flexible displays. We use a newly developed density-functional perturbation theory with a self-consistent Hubbard correction (DFPT+U) to study phonon-limited electron transport and phonon-assisted optical absorption in strained zinc oxide (ZnO). This parameter-free approach accounts for electron-phonon interactions and on-site correlation effects simultaneously. Electronic structures and phonon dispersions are computed under three distinct uniaxial strain directions. Uniaxial tensile strain up to 4.8% along [\bar110] is found to increase the room-temperature electron mobility by 19% while leaving visible-range optical absorption essentially unchanged. These results demonstrate that moderate strain can selectively enhance carrier transport without degrading optical transparenc...

items.title: Direct visualization of charge dynamics by Pockels imaging in optoelectronics
items.abstract: Understanding charge dynamics in optoelectronic devices is essential because it governs carrier transport, signal evolution, and device performance. Yet, experimental access to the spatiotemporal evolution of charge remains limited. Here, we introduce Carrier Dynamics by Pockels Imaging (CDPI), a sensitive, quantitative, and non-invasive pump-probe technique based on the linear electro-optic (Pockels) effect. CDPI images the electric-field wave associated with traveling photogenerated carriers and reveals the evolution of charge clouds in space and time. This provides direct access to fundamental transport processes, including drift, diffusion, carrier-carrier interactions, trapping, and detrapping. Furthermore, the internal conduction- and displacement-current profiles are obtained from the electric-field dynamics and shown to be consistent with the externally measured current transient...

items.title: 2D Transport in an in-plane magnetic field
items.abstract: A parallel in-plane magnetic field could, in principle, distinguish between two competing physical scenarios for the experimentally observed density-tuned 2D metal-insulator transition (where decreasing the carrier density leads to a crossover from an effective metal to an effective insulator): Wigner crystallization or Anderson localization. Since the main scattering mechanism in 2D doped semiconductors arises from screened random charged impurities and screening in turn depends on the electronic density of states, the in-plane magnetic field could distinguish between the two by decreasing screening through spin polarization and this enhances the effective critical density for Anderson localization compared with Wigner crystallization. items.title: Overcoming configuration bottleneck: Modular pathways to stable semiconductor spin-qubit arrays
items.abstract: Over the past decade, semiconductor spin qubits have progressed from few-qubit demonstrations toward larger-scale devices fabricated in increasingly reproducible academic and industrial processes. This progress marks an inflection point: the central challenge is no longer to demonstrate high-fidelity operation in carefully tuned devices but to discover, verify, and maintain stable operating conditions reliably across many interdependent controls, varied device geometries, and disparate material platforms. In this Perspective, we frame spin-qubit operation as a modular automation problem. We decompose the workflow into five modules: bootstrapping from minimal prior information, configuration tuning, virtualization of physical gates into effective control axes, qubit-level tuning, and an operation layer with drift-aware maintenance.
